Cause: The Thursday 02:00 reindex Job (catalog-reindex-29654040) is stuck in Active/NotReady (1/2). Its `reindex` container finished successfully at 02:41 Thursday (exit 0), but the `cloud-sql-proxy` container is defined as a regular container and keeps running, so the Pod never completes and the Job never finishes. Because the CronJob has `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, Friday 02:00's scheduled run was skipped — "if it is time for a new Job run and the previous Job run hasn't finished yet, the CronJob skips the new Job run" [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs#concurrency-policy-0]. The last successful reindex was Wednesday 02:00 (Job 29652600, image 4.1.3, single container). The image was bumped to 4.2.0 which added the cloud-sql-proxy sidecar as a normal container — that is what broke completion.

Evidence:
- Pod catalog-reindex-29654040-v8m2q: reindex container Terminated(Completed) 2026-05-20 02:41:17; cloud-sql-proxy still Running since 02:00:05; pod 1/2 Ready, Job Active for 2d6h.
- CronJob lastScheduleTime 2026-05-20T02:00:00Z, active=[29654040] — no new Job created for Friday because of Forbid.
- Previous day's pod (29652600, image 4.1.3) had only the `reindex` container and completed cleanly.

Fix (owner to apply): Convert `cloud-sql-proxy` from a regular container into a native sidecar by moving it under `spec.template.spec.initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`. "If you define a Job that uses sidecar using Kubernetes-style init containers, the sidecar container in each Pod does not prevent the Job from completing after the main container has finished." [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers#jobs-with-sidecar-containers-0] An example manifest is shown here [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers#jobs-with-sidecar-containers-1]. The node runs kubelet v1.30.4, where the SidecarContainers feature is enabled by default [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/_index#how-pods-manage-multiple-containers-2]. On termination, the kubelet will delay SIGTERM to the proxy until the reindex container exits [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#termination-with-sidecars-0]. Non-zero exit from the proxy on shutdown is expected and can be ignored [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers#differences-from-application-containers-0].

To unblock tonight's run immediately, also delete the stuck Job `catalog-reindex-29654040` (which will terminate its pod); the next 02:00 schedule will then be allowed to start. Jobs created by CronJobs should be idempotent [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/cron-jobs#job-creation-0], so re-running the reindex is safe.
